final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no genuinely new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That narrowing is analytically helpful, but it is not evidence. The existing evidence supports only this limited conclusion: aggregate readiness and rehearsal performance support general deployment readiness, while the HR benefits enrollment issue remains an unresolved weakness in a named launch use case. Under the stated policy, that weakness must either be disclosed before launch or be covered by approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation details. The record still lacks admissible proof of any of those compliance predicates, and the current model-card draft affirmatively says there are no known material limitations. That is why this is not yet compliant_with_caveats. A caveated position would require evidence that the caveat was actually implemented in the model card or otherwise formally approved, not merely argued for.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the final model card was updated to disclose the HR benefits enrollment limitation for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
The current model-card draft still says there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the unresolved HR benefits issue.
The draft runbook remains governance-incomplete and does not satisfy the policy condition for certification without material caveats.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results support general launch readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate for this unresolved use-case weakness.
